role: Solutions Architect III, Internal Audit Data Analytics
responsibilities: Own the integration architecture across BI/Analytics, Applied Science, and Data Engineering sub-teams, designing the pipeline that connects analytical tooling, risk models, and data infrastructure into a unified testing workflow.

Write SQL, build ETL/ELT processes, create data models, and implement agentic workflows using LLM orchestration and tool-use chains with human-in-the-loop validation to move audit testing from reactive to proactive.

Investigate architectural constraints and competing priorities across sub-teams, drive alignment on data models and pipeline patterns, and resolve technical disagreements through hands-on analysis rather than positional authority.
Author 6-pagers, technical design documents, and reference architectures; present architecture decisions and trade-offs to Director and VP-level audiences within Internal Audit leadership.
Define reusable patterns for agentic audit pipelines that surface risk, generate test procedures, and speed up engagement execution across the enterprise.

evidence.velocity_vs_rigour: implement agentic workflows using LLM orchestration and tool-use chains with human-in-the-loop validation
evidence.velocity_vs_rigour_explanation: Audit coverage, risk models and human-in-the-loop validation frame the work; "speed up engagement execution" is the one speed phrase and it describes the outcome for auditors.
evidence.domain_risk: Your customers are Internal Audit's audit teams — the people who carry testing to the business and assure risk coverage across the enterprise.
evidence.domain_risk_explanation: The pipeline generates the test procedures that assure enterprise risk coverage for Amazon's Internal Audit function.
evidence.collaboration_width: BI/Analytics; Applied Science; Data Engineering sub-teams; audit teams; Internal Audit leadership
evidence.data_team_maturity: Three sub-teams (BI/Analytics, Applied Science, and Data Engineering) each bring specialized capabilities, and this role exists to integrate them into a single testing pipeline.
evidence.data_team_maturity_explanation: Three named sub-teams with distinct charters, each already running its own dashboards, risk models and pipelines.
evidence.jd_authorship: You might start by reviewing a data pipeline prototype with the Data Engineering sub-team, working through schema decisions that affect downstream risk models.
evidence.jd_authorship_explanation: The posting includes a literal day-in-the-life and names the specific integration failure — "Dashboards don't feed into risk models".
evidence.stakeholder_orientation: Your customers are Internal Audit's audit teams
evidence.stakeholder_orientation_explanation: The role's named customers are the internal audit function and its Director and VP leadership.
evidence.autonomy_level: You will own the integration strategy that brings these pieces together.
evidence.autonomy_level_explanation: The role owns the strategy, makes the technical calls, and is "defining the patterns rather than following an existing playbook".
evidence.ai_role: Define reusable patterns for agentic audit pipelines that surface risk, generate test procedures, and speed up engagement execution across the enterprise.
evidence.ai_role_explanation: The candidate builds the agentic pipelines and LLM orchestration that run on the data infrastructure they design.
evidence.testing_framing: No testing or data quality signal anywhere in the JD.
evidence.testing_framing_explanation: "Testing" throughout means audit test procedures; no data quality, data contract or observability practice appears.
evidence.loss_aversion_framing: The target state is agentic pipelines that surface risk and generate test procedures before teams even open an engagement.
evidence.loss_aversion_framing_explanation: Risk coverage and audit assurance are the role's entire purpose, stated from the first paragraph onward.
evidence.greenfield_vs_fix: These tools work well independently, but they haven't been integrated into a single testing pipeline
evidence.greenfield_vs_fix_explanation: Integrating tooling that several teams already built sits alongside defining agentic patterns that do not yet exist.
evidence.loss_aversion: "assure risk coverage across the enterprise" — the pipeline exists so audit teams can cover enterprise risk, which is the whole framing of the role.
